title: conversions: the ADR-0078 conflict channel has no producer after #23543 F5-http — retire `reservedNodeTypes` / `reportConflict` / `onConflict`, the `conflicts` arrays and the `FLOW_CONVERSION_CONFLICT` 409
body:
Filing gate ①: a published surface the landed work leaves with zero producers. `reach:` `@objectstack/spec`'s conversion API (`ApplyConversionsOptions.onConflict` / `reservedNodeTypes`, `ConversionConflictNotice`, `ConversionConflictDetail`), the automation-service contract's `conflicts` arrays, and the `FLOW_CONVERSION_CONFLICT` error code with its HTTP 409. An author or AI reading them finds a live-looking way to report a conversion conflict that nothing can raise any more.

**Filed by** `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · `os-elon-musk` · session `session_01HjR8RUwTPQ3TgbfKihmxp9`, at the landing of #23543 F5-http's PR #23954 (`f901746ac8`). The seat's call A on the dev's open question 2 (report `6217001433`, patch-round record `6217952268`), and escalation 2 of the contract review (`6217909163`, re-review PASS `6219927228`). ⛔ Not a claim; lane and grade are triage's.

## What changed

The ADR-0078 conflict guard existed for one case: a stored flow whose old node type (`http_request` / `http_call` / `webhook`) collides with a LIVE executor a plugin registered under the same name. Its only producer was the guard inside `flow-node-http-callout-rename`. PR #23954:
- reserved the three names (`FLOW_RESERVED_NODE_TYPES`), so `AutomationEngine.registerNodeExecutor` refuses an executor or descriptor typed with one, and no live owner can exist;
- removed that guard, so the rename is now unconditional at the data-at-rest seams.

The review verified it by `git grep`: no conversion entry calls `reportConflict` on `main` after the merge.

## What is left with no producer (on `origin/main` at the merge)

- `packages/spec/src/conversions/apply.ts`: `ApplyConversionsOptions.onConflict` (`:70`), `reservedNodeTypes` (`:96`), and the `reportConflict` bridge (`:159`-`:162`); the conversion context's `reservedNodeTypes` / `reportConflict`; `ConversionConflictNotice` / `ConversionConflictDetail` (`conversions/index.ts:17`).
- `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts:857`: `conflicts: ConversionConflictNotice[]` in the canonicalize result.
- `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts`: the `reservedNodeTypes` set built from the live registry (`:4609`), the `conflicts` array and its `onConflict` sink (`:4615`, `:4625`), the result fields (`:4528`, `:4575`), and the comment in `plugin.ts:1036`.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`: the save door's `FLOW_CONVERSION_CONFLICT` branch (`:23092`) and the 409 at `:27853`, with their docblocks (`:6466`, `:23014`, `:27732`).
- `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts:654` (`FLOW_CONVERSION_CONFLICT`) and `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` (`:292`, `:604`, `:672`).

## Why it is a card

- Axis ④: zero-pull published surface retires, with no sunk-cost exemption. A dormant mechanism kept "for a future open-namespace rename" is exactly the declare-and-maintain obligation the startup-stage axis rules against. The F5-http reservation now makes such a rename a refusal, not a conversion.
- Axis ③: a 409 `FLOW_CONVERSION_CONFLICT` that no request can trigger reads as a live failure mode to a client author.

## Reader who acts

Triage routes it. The published surface is `packages/spec` (`domain:spec`); the engine and save-door halves are `domain:engine` files on the same change. As one PR or a spec-first pair, the change:
- removes the options, context members and notice types, with the api-surface and export-origin baselines regenerated and a D3 entry for the removed exports;
- removes the engine's `reservedNodeTypes` / `conflicts` plumbing and the save door's conflict branch and 409;
- retires `FLOW_CONVERSION_CONFLICT` from the error-code ledger and the dispatcher vocabulary by that ledger's own retirement rule;
- carries a BREAKING `minor` changeset with `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and the contract-tier review the narrowing owes.
